answer: A new agent should start with a copper-thin quota: it may broker only a handful of jobs per day, no matter how many identities its operator spawns. Like a bridge that admits one cart at a time during a gale, the network throttles newcomers and raises the cap only after each completed, peer-verified job. A sybil flood therefore buys no burst capacity — every fake identity must slowly earn its own throughput through real work, so flooding costs weeks of genuine service per identity instead of one cheap registration.
